history.summary: SUB-SHRINE / RELATED ENTRY: this CSV row is not an independent temple but the Ganapathy shrine(s) within the Vaikom Mahadeva Temple complex — see seq 1776 (id: vaikom-mahadeva-temple). The complex contains several Ganapathy prathishtas: a Vighneswara Prathishta on a stone peedhom in the south-east corner outside the sreekovil; Maha Ganapathy in the south and Sakthy Ganapathy in the north (both panchaloha idols); and Sthamba Vinayaka in the southern courtyard, believed to have protected the temple complex from evil forces ever since Sage Parasurama consecrated the temple. The CSV name is generic and may refer to any or all of these shrines; identity of which shrine is intended is AMBIGUOUS (verify). Worship here follows the main temple's rituals, with Ganapathy homam among the regular offerings.

name: Ganapathy shrine, Vaikom temple complex
town_description: Vaikom is a historic town in Kottayam district, Kerala, on the eastern banks of the Vembanad Lake and its backwaters. It is famous for the Vaikom Mahadeva Temple, the Vaikom Satyagraha temple-entry movement of 1924-25, and its serene waterways. The town lies roughly 30 km from Kottayam and is well connected by road to Ernakulam and Kottayam.
tradition: Hinduism (Shaivism; Ganapatya sub-tradition within the complex)
